Ingliz tilida «boʻlmoq» feʼli tushib qolmaydi: «Men talabaman» = [[I am a student.]]

OlmoshFeʼlQisqa
[[I]][[am]][[I'm]]
[[he]] / [[she]] / [[it]][[is]][[he's]]
[[we]] / [[you]] / [[they]][[are]][[we're]]

Inkor: [[I am not]], [[she isn't]]. Savol: feʼl oldinga chiqadi: [[Are you a student?]]

body.uz:
[[a]] (unli oldidan [[an]]) — birinchi marta tilga olingan birlik narsa: [[a book]], [[an apple]]. [[the]] — maʼlum narsa: [[The book is on the table.]]

Koʻplik odatda [[-s]]: [[book]] → [[books]]. Notoʻgʻrilari: [[man]] → [[men]], [[child]] → [[children]].

Inkor va savol [[did]] bilan, feʼl esa asos shaklda: [[I didn't go.]], [[Did you see it?]]

She bought a new dress.|U yangi koʻylak sotib oldi.

title.uz: Kelasi zamon: will va going to

body.uz:
[[going to]] — oldindan rejalashtirilgan ish: [[I'm going to visit Samarkand.]]

[[will]] — shu zahoti qilingan qaror, vaʼda, bashorat: [[I'll call you later.]], [[It will rain tomorrow.]]

It will be sunny tomorrow.|Ertaga quyoshli boʻladi.

body.uz:
[[am / is / are]] + feʼl + [[-ing]]: [[I am reading.]] = Hozir oʻqiyapman.

Solishtiring: [[I work every day.]] (odat) — [[I'm working now.]] (hozir).

grammar.ex:

body.uz:
Qisqa sifatlar: [[-er]] / [[the -est]]: [[big]] → [[bigger]] → [[the biggest]]. Uzun sifatlar: [[more]] / [[the most]]: [[more interesting]]. «…dan» = [[than]]: [[Moscow is bigger than Tashkent.]]

Notoʻgʻri: [[good]] → [[better]] → [[the best]], [[bad]] → [[worse]] → [[the worst]].

This book is more interesting.|Bu kitob qiziqroq.

readings.title: The City of the Future
readings.sents:
What will the city of the future be like?|Kelajak shahri qanday boʻladi?
Many experts think it will have more greenery and fewer cars.|Koʻp mutaxassislar unda koʻkalamzorlar koʻp, mashinalar kam boʻladi deb oʻylaydi.
People will travel by electric cars and bicycles.|Odamlar elektromobillar va velosipedlarda yuradi.
Homes will get energy from the sun and wind.|Uylar energiyani quyosh va shamoldan oladi.
Smart systems will control light and heat.|Aqlli tizimlar yorugʻlik va issiqlikni boshqaradi.
However, this idea also has critics.|Biroq bu gʻoyaning tanqidchilari ham bor.
They say such technologies are too expensive.|Ular bunday texnologiyalar juda qimmat deyishadi.
Besides, not everyone is ready to change their habits.|Bundan tashqari, hamma ham odatlarini oʻzgartirishga tayyor emas.
It's hard to say who is right.|Kim haq ekanini aytish qiyin.
But one thing is clear: a city must be comfortable for people.|Ammo bir narsa aniq: shahar odamlar uchun qulay boʻlishi kerak.

We learn the news faster than before.|Yangiliklarni avvalgidan tezroq bilib olamiz.
However, social networks also have a downside.|Biroq ijtimoiy tarmoqlarning salbiy tomoni ham bor.
Many people spend several hours a day on their phones.|Koʻp odamlar kuniga bir necha soatni telefonda oʻtkazadi.
This affects sleep, studies and mood.|Bu uyqu, oʻqish va kayfiyatga taʼsir qiladi.

Psychologists advise taking breaks.|Psixologlar tanaffus qilishni maslahat beradi.

title.uz: Nisbiy gaplar: who, which, that, whose

body.uz:
[[who]] — odamlar, [[which]] — narsalar, [[that]] — ikkalasi uchun, [[whose]] — kimning: [[The woman who called is my aunt.]], [[The book which I bought…]], [[the man whose car…]]

readings.title: Reading in the Digital Age
readings.sents:
Lately many people complain that people have stopped reading.|Soʻnggi paytlarda koʻpchilik odamlar kitob oʻqimay qoʻydi deb noliydi.
However, research shows a more complex picture.|Biroq tadqiqotlar murakkabroq manzarani koʻrsatmoqda.
We read no less than before, but we read differently.|Biz avvalgidan kam oʻqimaymiz, lekin boshqacha oʻqiymiz.
Texts have become shorter, and attention more scattered.|Matnlar qisqaroq, diqqat esa tarqoqroq boʻlib qoldi.
Thus, it is not the quantity but the depth of reading that suffers.|Shunday qilib, oʻqishning miqdori emas, chuqurligi zarar koʻrmoqda.
Scientists emphasize that the ability to concentrate is a skill.|Olimlar diqqatni jamlash qobiliyati — bu koʻnikma ekanini taʼkidlaydi.
Like any skill, it needs to be trained.|Har qanday koʻnikma kabi uni mashq qildirish kerak.
For example, it is useful to read paper books without a phone nearby.|Masalan, qogʻoz kitoblarni yonida telefon boʻlmagan holda oʻqish foydali.
On the whole, digital technologies are not harmful in themselves.|Umuman olganda, raqamli texnologiyalarning oʻzi zararli emas.
Everything depends on how we use them.|Hammasi ulardan qanday foydalanishimizga bogʻliq.

readings.title: Sustainable Development
readings.sents:
The concept of sustainable development appeared at the end of the twentieth century.|Barqaror rivojlanish konsepsiyasi yigirmanchi asr oxirida paydo boʻlgan.
Its essence is simple: meet today's needs without harming future generations.|Uning mohiyati oddiy: kelajak avlodlarga zarar yetkazmasdan bugungi ehtiyojlarni qondirish.
However, in practice this turned out to be much more difficult.|Biroq amalda bu ancha murakkab boʻlib chiqdi.
Economic growth often contradicts environmental protection.|Iqtisodiy oʻsish koʻpincha atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishga zid keladi.
Nevertheless, many countries are introducing "green" technologies.|Shunga qaramay, koʻplab mamlakatlar «yashil» texnologiyalarni joriy etmoqda.
Companies also take environmental factors into account.|Kompaniyalar ham ekologik omillarni hisobga olmoqda.
Undoubtedly, without the participation of each of us there will be no success.|Shubhasiz, har birimizning ishtirokimizsiz muvaffaqiyat boʻlmaydi.

readings.title: The Art of Arguing
readings.sents:
The ability to argue is one of the most important in the modern world.|Bahslasha olish — zamonaviy dunyodagi eng muhim qobiliyatlardan biri.
The goal of an argument is not to defeat the other person but to get closer to the truth.|Bahsning maqsadi suhbatdoshni yengish emas, balki haqiqatga yaqinlashishdir.
First of all, you need to listen carefully to your opponent.|Eng avvalo, raqibni diqqat bilan tinglash kerak.
Then you should give arguments, not emotions.|Keyin hissiyotlarni emas, dalillarni keltirish kerak.
It is important to distinguish facts from opinions.|Faktlarni fikrlardan ajrata bilish muhim.
If you are wrong, admit it — it's a sign of strength, not weakness.|Agar notoʻgʻri boʻlsangiz, tan oling — bu zaiflik emas, kuch belgisi.
Ultimately, a good argument enriches both sides.|Oxir-oqibat, yaxshi bahs ikkala tomonni ham boyitadi.

His zeal knew no bounds.|Uning gʻayratining chegarasi yoʻq edi.
Everything in this world is transient.|Bu dunyoda hamma narsa foniy.
Her patience ran out.|Uning sabri tugadi.
She unraveled his plan.|U uning rejasini fosh qildi.
Having weighed all the pros and cons, he refused.|Barcha afzallik va kamchiliklarni oʻlchab koʻrib, u rad etdi.
A strange premonition came over me.|Meni gʻalati bir koʻngil sezishi qamrab oldi.
In the twilight the city looked ghostly.|Gʻira-shira qorongʻilikda shahar sharpadek koʻrinardi.
Happiness is fleeting, like spring rain.|Baxt bahor yomgʻiridek oʻtkinchi.
His taste was distinguished by refinement.|Uning didi nafisligi bilan ajralib turardi.
Compassion is not weakness.|Rahmdillik — zaiflik emas.
She confided her innermost thoughts to him.|U unga eng ichki fikrlarini ishonib aytdi.
All his efforts proved futile.|Uning barcha urinishlari befoyda boʻlib chiqdi.
We bow before his talent.|Biz uning isteʼdodi oldida bosh egamiz.
A pre-dawn silence fell.|Tong oldi sukunati choʻkdi.
He chose his path in youth.|U oʻz yoʻlini yoshligida tanladi.
The chronicle preserves the memory of those events.|Solnoma oʻsha voqealar xotirasini saqlaydi.
Our job is to do our duty.|Bizning ishimiz — burchimizni bajarish.
This book is an intricate web of fates.|Bu kitob — taqdirlarning chigal toʻri.
His speech was chaotic.|Uning nutqi tartibsiz edi.
He had an epiphany.|Uning koʻzi ochildi.
Beauty will save the world.|Goʻzallik dunyoni qutqaradi.
Life is not a walk in the park.|Hayot — gulzorda sayr emas.
Better late than never.|Hech qachondan koʻra kech boʻlsa ham yaxshi.
A drowning man clutches at a straw.|Choʻkayotgan odam xasga ham yopishadi.
There's no smoke without fire.|Shamol boʻlmasa, daraxtning boshi qimirlamaydi.
Business before pleasure.|Avval ish, keyin oʻyin.
A friend in need is a friend indeed.|Doʻst boshga kulfat tushganda bilinadi.

readings.title: The Art of Silence
readings.sents:
They say that speech is silver, but silence is gold.|Soʻz kumush boʻlsa, sukut oltin, deyishadi.
In the age of endless messages, this proverb sounds almost like a challenge.|Cheksiz xabarlar asrida bu maqol deyarli daʼvatdek yangraydi.
We rush to answer, comment, have our say.|Biz javob berishga, izoh qoldirishga, fikr bildirishga shoshilamiz.
And rarely wonder whether it was worth it.|Va kamdan-kam bunga arziganmi, deb oʻylaymiz.
Meanwhile, the ability to keep silent at the right moment is a sign not of weakness but of maturity.|Holbuki, kerakli paytda jim tura olish zaiflik emas, balki yetuklik belgisidir.
Silence gives time to make sense of what was heard.|Sukut eshitganlarimizni mushohada qilish uchun vaqt beradi.
It turns out that listening is no less important than speaking.|Maʼlum boʻlishicha, tinglash gapirishdan kam muhim emas.
It is no coincidence that sages of all ages valued taciturnity.|Barcha zamonlarning donishmandlari kamgaplikni qadrlagani bejiz emas.

readings.title: On Translation
readings.sents:
Translation is not a simple replacement of words.|Tarjima — soʻzlarni oddiygina almashtirish emas.
Every language holds within itself a special vision of the world.|Har bir til oʻzida dunyoga alohida qarashni saqlaydi.
Idioms, wordplay, subtext — all this is hard to translate.|Iboralar, soʻz oʻyinlari, ichki maʼno — bularning barchasini tarjima qilish qiyin.
A translator has to choose between accuracy and beauty.|Tarjimon aniqlik va goʻzallik oʻrtasida tanlov qilishiga toʻgʻri keladi.
No wonder they say a translator is a co-author.|Tarjimonni hammuallif deyishlari bejiz emas.
A good translation preserves not only the meaning but also the spirit of the original.|Yaxshi tarjima nafaqat maʼnoni, balki asl nusxaning ruhini ham saqlaydi.
That is precisely why great books are translated again and again.|Aynan shuning uchun buyuk kitoblar qayta-qayta tarjima qilinadi.

readings.title: The Memory of a Place
readings.sents:
There are cities that live in us long after we have left them.|Shunday shaharlar borki, biz ulardan ketganimizdan keyin ham uzoq vaqt ichimizda yashaydi.
The smell of rain on an old street, the ringing of bells, the voice of a merchant at the market.|Eski koʻchadagi yomgʻir hidi, qoʻngʻiroqlar jarangi, bozordagi savdogarning ovozi.
All this suddenly surfaces in memory.|Bularning barchasi toʻsatdan xotirada jonlanadi.
Nostalgia is not just longing for the past.|Nostalgiya — shunchaki oʻtmishni sogʻinish emas.
It is an attempt to bring back a part of yourself that stayed there.|Bu — u yerda qolib ketgan oʻzligingning bir qismini qaytarishga urinish.
Returning there years later, we often recognize neither the city nor ourselves.|Yillar oʻtib u yerga qaytganimizda, koʻpincha na shaharni, na oʻzimizni taniymiz.
And yet this meeting gives a strange serenity.|Shunga qaramay, bu uchrashuv gʻalati bir osoyishtalik bagʻishlaydi.

dialogues.lines:
A|So, did you finish the novel?|Xoʻsh, romanni oʻqib tugatdingmi?
B|I did. Honestly, the ending baffled me.|Tugatdim. Rostini aytsam, yakuni meni esankiratib qoʻydi.
A|Yes, the author likes to leave things unsaid.|Ha, muallif gapni oxiriga yetkazmaslikni yaxshi koʻradi.
B|Exactly. Everything rests on the subtext.|Aynan. Hammasi ichki maʼnoga asoslangan.
A|But what language! I couldn't put it down.|Lekin tili qanday! Qoʻlimdan qoʻya olmadim.
B|That's true, no arguing.|Bu toʻgʻri, bahslashib boʻlmaydi.

A|Are you still offended with me?|Hali ham mendan xafamisan?
B|Not so much offended as disappointed.|Xafa emas, koʻproq hafsalam pir boʻldi.
A|I understand. I lost my temper and said too much.|Tushunaman. Jahl ustida ortiqcha gapirib yubordim.
B|A word is not a sparrow; once it flies out, you can't catch it.|Otilgan oʻq qaytmas, aytilgan soʻz qaytmas.
A|I know. Please forgive me.|Bilaman. Iltimos, meni kechir.
B|All right, let bygones be bygones.|Mayli, oʻtgan ishga salovat.
A|Thank you. You're a true friend.|Rahmat. Sen haqiqiy doʻstsan.

A|What do you say about this canvas?|Bu kartina haqida nima deysan?
B|The colors are striking, but the composition is overloaded, in my opinion.|Rangi hayratlanarli, lekin menimcha, kompozitsiyasi juda yuklangan.
A|And I think that's exactly the artist's intention.|Menimcha esa, rassomning niyati aynan shunda.
B|Possibly. Chaos as a reflection of the era?|Ehtimol. Tartibsizlik — davr aksi sifatidami?
A|Exactly. Look at the brushstrokes — how much anxiety there is in them.|Aynan. Moʻyqalam izlariga qara — ularda qanchalik xavotir bor.
B|You've almost convinced me.|Meni deyarli ishontirding.
